response: Yes, inhaled steroids and cromones differ in their effects on hospital admission rates for asthma in children. Studies have shown that inhaled corticosteroids are more effective than cromones in reducing hospital admission rates for asthma in children. Inhaled corticosteroids have been found to be more potent anti-inflammatory agents, which can lead to better control of asthma symptoms and a lower risk of hospitalization. Cromones, on the other hand, are less potent and may be more suitable for mild asthma or as add-on therapy. Overall, the evidence suggests that inhaled corticosteroids are a more effective treatment option for reducing hospital admission rates for asthma in children compared to cromones.
